A.summary: A single-parent chain of OpNodes, each asking its operation for an input rect and then computing missing cells one at a time with the whole-grid formula (compute_cell reading absolute coordinates through ctx.get). Each node memoises computed cells as row spans plus a (y,x) dict, so overlapping windows and evaluate_many share work without tiles, and reset_counters drops every cache.
forces_resolved: exactness against economy: the evaluator only chooses which cells get the per-cell formula, never how they are computed, so window results are bit-identical to whole results (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:276-282, impl-A/stencilpipe/ops.py:149-162; checked: 0/941 box cells differ after add)
border rule only at the real border: kernels clamp against ctx.in_extent, not a buffer (impl-A/stencilpipe/ops.py:150-155, 175-178)

small requests against shared work: the _Spans per-row interval memo computes and counts each cell once across overlapping windows, with no rounding to tiles (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:32-93, 255-256; checked: two overlapping 10x10 windows cost 175 cells, not 200)
local against global: normalize declares the whole input as its footprint and caches the max once per node in prepare/_state (impl-A/stencilpipe/ops.py:214-228, impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:270-271)
measurements are window requests, not a bounding box: evaluate_many ensures each rect on its own (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:390-394)
keep the best case: a window already covered by the memo costs nothing (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:255-256)
forces_in_tension: declared against discovered reach: an under-declared read raises only when the parent is an OpNode (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:284-291); reads from a SourceNode always succeed (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:187-193), and cells memoised by earlier windows hide a short footprint

memory: every computed cell is a tuple-keyed dict entry kept until reset_counters (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:223, 401-410), so a whole evaluation holds far more memory than rows of floats and the cache is never evicted
forces_unnoticed: tile size against reach (no tiles; the span memo makes them less needed, but this is never stated)
the cost rule (evaluate whole when footprints cost about the whole) is absent; with per-cell computation it has no role, but nothing says so

A.best_thing: Compute each output cell with the whole-grid formula over absolute coordinates, and memoise per node by row spans: this gives exactness and overlap sharing with no Buffer, origin or tile machinery.
A.worst_thing: Source reads are unguarded and the memo masks short footprints, so the invariance tests are the only thing standing between a wrong input_rect and silently wrong edges.

B.summary: A registry of stateless Op singletons, each declaring footprint(window, index, extent, args, scale) and a windowed run() over origin-carrying Buffers that raise FootprintError on any read outside the declared footprint. The evaluator follows the chapter's flowchart literally (whole cache, WHOLE or 0.6 cost rule, clipped footprints, window cache), and normalize is built as divide(img, max_stat(img)).
forces_resolved: exactness against economy: kernels read through Buffer in document coordinates and clamp against the node's real extent (impl-B/stencilpipe/buffers.py:27-103, impl-B/stencilpipe/ops.py:103, 130); bit-identical to whole results (checked)

declared against discovered reach: every read, including from sources (impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:247), goes through a buffer cut to the footprint, and reads outside it raise FootprintError (impl-B/stencilpipe/buffers.py:66-103), with negative-control tests (impl-B/tests/test_regions.py:172-235)
local against global: normalize is split into a WHOLE-footprint MaxStat node and a local Divide node, with the 1x1 statistic cached in _whole (impl-B/stencilpipe/ops.py:178-245)
cost rule: a node is evaluated whole when its footprints exceed whole_fraction of its inputs, and the fraction is a setting (impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:282-298, 112)
keep the best case: the whole value is cut first (impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:252-254)
reaches add up along a chain: each node widens its own request (impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:300-310), tested at impl-B/tests/test_regions.py:55-62
forces_in_tension: small requests against shared work: the window cache is keyed by the exact window (impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:256-258, 272) and evaluate_many just loops (impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:201-207), so overlapping windows recompute the overlap (checked: 200 cells for two 10x10 windows sharing 25)

B.best_thing: Hand every kernel, sources included, a buffer cut to its declared footprint and make reads outside it raise; together with the negative-control tests this turns a short reach from a silent edge bug into a failure.
B.worst_thing: Machinery transcribed from the sketch with no user (scale conversion, composite/internal flags, listing helpers) makes up a large share of the package and already disagrees with the kernels.

C.summary: Each evaluate builds a one-shot _Solution: a demand phase propagates input_region rects consumer-to-producer in topological order, and a compute phase fills a per-solution sparse store cell by cell with the whole-grid formula, counting each cell once. Nothing is cached between calls, and normalize demands its whole input and recomputes the max in prepare every time.
forces_resolved: exactness against economy: per-cell formula over absolute coordinates (impl-C/stencilpipe/ops.py:122-135, impl-C/stencilpipe/engine.py:157-166); bit-identical (checked)
border rule at the real border: kernels clamp on ctx.in_extent (impl-C/stencilpipe/ops.py:123-128, 147-148)

small requests against shared work within one request: evaluate_many unions demands per node and skips already-stored cells (impl-C/stencilpipe/engine.py:146-166, 300-314; checked: 175 cells for two overlapping 10x10 windows)
measurements are window requests, not a bounding box: rects are kept separately and only contained ones are dropped (impl-C/stencilpipe/regions.py:64-86)
reaches add up along a chain: the demand phase widens at every node (impl-C/stencilpipe/engine.py:131-143)
forces_in_tension: keep the best case: every evaluate starts a fresh _Solution (impl-C/stencilpipe/engine.py:296), so a second window of the same view recomputes everything, and a test makes this a law (impl-C/tests/test_stencilpipe.py:333-344)
local against global: normalize is not split; it demands its whole input and recomputes the max on every call (impl-C/stencilpipe/ops.py:187-199)

declared against discovered reach: a store miss raises KeyError (impl-C/stencilpipe/engine.py:115), but sources are read directly (impl-C/stencilpipe/engine.py:113-114), and overlapping demanded rects can hide a short footprint
forces_unnoticed: the cost rule (not needed per cell, but never discussed)

C.best_thing: Separating demand (which rects each node needs) from compute (fill them once) makes the footprint propagation readable in about 40 lines and gives batch sharing for free.
C.worst_thing: Without any cache, normalize recomputes the whole input on every call, and the test suite locks that in.

D.summary: A content-keyed graph of op objects with plain-tuple windows. A buffer evaluator follows the chapter's flow (whole cache, then a bounded containing-window cache, then WHOLE or cost fallback, then per-input footprints), and normalize takes its max through a global_params hook into engine.statistic. Kernels index raw buffer rows with origin arithmetic repeated in each op, and box uses a summed-area table over its buffer.
forces_resolved: local against global: Normalize.global_params gets a cached whole-input max from engine.statistic, and windows pass through the division (impl-D/stencilpipe/ops.py:272-287, impl-D/stencilpipe/engine.py:203-219)
keep the best case: the whole cache, then a containing cached window, is cut before computing (impl-D/stencilpipe/engine.py:230-236, 298-304)
cost rule: footprints over 0.6 of the inputs fall back to whole (impl-D/stencilpipe/engine.py:289-296)
border rule at the real border: kernels clamp on ctx.in_extents (impl-D/stencilpipe/ops.py:152, 174-175, 203)
forces_in_tension: exactness against economy: box's summed-area table over the buffer (impl-D/stencilpipe/ops.py:159-190) makes each value depend on the buffer origin. Checked: 872 of 941 windowed box cells differ bitwise from the whole result. Tolerance in the tests hides it (impl-D/tests/support.py:113-116)

measurements are window requests, not a bounding box: evaluate_many goes whole when the union bbox exceeds 0.6 of the node (impl-D/stencilpipe/engine.py:178-182). Checked: two 4x4 windows at opposite corners of a 400x300 box/dx chain compute all 240,000 cells
small requests against shared work: only fully containing cached windows are reused, so partial overlaps recompute (checked: 200 cells for two 10x10 windows sharing 25)

generativity.notes: All five share the deep structure: a declared footprint per op, propagated and clipped at each node, so reaches add up for free. They split on where the kernel stands. A and C compute cell by cell over absolute coordinates, which makes exactness and overlap sharing structural and makes Buffer, origin, WHOLE and the cost rule unnecessary. B, D and E compute windows over origin-carrying buffers and transcribe the chapter's flowchart step by step, including the 0.6 constant. Within that group B and E are closest (Window class, WHOLE, statistic as a node, exact-window cache); D uses tuples and a hook. The details differ in exactly the places the chapter is vague: how the statistic is wired in (three shapes), whether sources are cut to the footprint (only B), and whether evaluate_many respects separate neighbourhoods (D does not).

worse_is_better: A, and C more so, reach the essential quality with less: bit-exact windows, footprint propagation and batch sharing, with no Buffer or origin class, no WHOLE sentinel, no cost threshold and no scale conversion. Per-cell evaluation over absolute coordinates makes the chapter's buffer-origin consequence and the cost rule irrelevant, and A's span memo shares overlapping windows better than any buffer implementation (175 vs 200 cells). B, D and E carry buffers and origins (needed only because they chose window kernels), a copied 0.6 threshold, content keys and, in B, a scale apparatus the task never uses. Of that extra, only B's footprint guard and an explicit statistic node earn their place. The buffer route is also where exactness was lost (D, E prefix sums). A's real gaps are an unguarded source read and per-cell dict memory. C's gap is the missing cache.
chapter_lessons: Exactness is broken by more than a short footprint. Kernels whose arithmetic depends on the buffer origin, such as prefix sums or summed-area tables (impl-D/stencilpipe/ops.py:159-190, impl-E/stencilpipe/ops.py:112-136), make windows differ from whole results even when the footprint is correct. Tolerance-based invariance tests hide this (impl-D/tests/support.py:113, impl-E/tests/test_invariance.py:91). The chapter should demand exact equality in the invariance test and warn that each output cell must be computed in an order that does not depend on the buffer origin.

Name the footprint guard as the cheap answer to 'declared against discovered reach': cut every input, sources included, to the declared footprint and raise on reads outside it. Only B did this (impl-B/stencilpipe/buffers.py:66-103, impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:247). A, C and E give kernels the whole source (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:187-193, impl-C/stencilpipe/engine.py:113-114, impl-E/stencilpipe/engine.py:251-252), so a short reach directly above a source goes unnoticed.

The cost rule invites the note-10 trap. D applied 'cost about the whole' to the bounding box of several windows (impl-D/stencilpipe/engine.py:178-182) and computes the whole grid for two scattered probes. The chapter should say the rule is per node and per window, never across a request's bounding box, and that the 0.6 in the sketch is a placeholder: B, D and E all copied it unmeasured.

Mark the units/scale machinery as conditional. B copied the sketch's scale conversion into a task with no scale (impl-B/stencilpipe/registry.py:31-59, impl-B/stencilpipe/engine.py:113-115), and it already disagrees with the kernel (impl-B/stencilpipe/ops.py:93-101).

Say how the statistic node is wired. The phrase produced three shapes: graph nodes (impl-B/stencilpipe/ops.py:241-245), a parameter hook (impl-D/stencilpipe/ops.py:272-273) and a hidden node in op state that needs bind, global_dependencies and ctx.value (impl-E/stencilpipe/ops.py:255-264). Recommend making the statistic an ordinary input of the local half, divide(img, stat(img)), so the evaluator needs no special case.

Offer per-cell demand with a memo as a variation alongside tiles. A shares overlapping work exactly, with no rounding (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:32-93), and A and C need neither the buffer-origin consequence nor the cost rule. The chapter presents tiles as the only answer to 'small requests against shared work', and should also name the memory cost of per-cell caches (impl-A/stencilpipe/engine.py:223).

Cache-first and cost measurement interact. A and B clear their caches on reset_counters, while D and E keep them, so the same request reports different costs. C rejects caching outright and writes a test for it (impl-C/tests/test_stencilpipe.py:333-344). The chapter should say how a cache coexists with measuring cost, for example with a cold mode for measurement.
